Sarah's hair was long. Now it is very short.Present Perfect: Sarah has cut her hair.Present Simple: Sarah cuts her hair to feel good. Present Continuous: Sarah is cutting her hair at the the beauty / hair salon.Simple Past: Sarah cut her hair yesterday.Past Continuous: Sarah was cutting her hair while her mother was doing her nails.Sarah was cutting her hair when I arrived. Sarah was cutting her hair at 3.00 pm.2. The floor was dirty. Now it is clean.Present Perfect: The floor has been cleaned. – O chão foi limpo (by my sister)My sister has cleaned the floor. – Minha irmã limpou o chão.Present Simple: My sister cleans the floor once a week to help me.Present Continuous: My sister is cleaning the floor today.Past Simple: My sister cleaned the floor last night.Past Continuous: My sister was cleaning the floor when I arrived (at) home. 3. Mark's car isn’t in his garage. He is walking to work.Present Perfect: Mark has sold his car. Present Simple: Mark sells cars as his job.Every time Mark walks to work he sees interesting cars to buy.Past Continuous: Mark was walking to work when he saw several interesting cars to buy.Present Continuous: Mark is selling cars below market price / at a discount.Past Simple: Mark sold his car two weeks ago.4. The oven is warm and there is a cake on the table.Present Perfect: My mother has cooked /baked a cake.5. They are standing outside because they don't have their keys.Present Perfect: They have lost their keys.6. The ground is wet and there are puddles everywhere.Present Perfect: It has rained.7. I am not hungry anymore. My plate is empty.Present Perfect: I have eaten all the food. I have had lunch. 8. The TV is off and the room is quiet.Present Perfect: My dad has slept. My dad has gone to bed.My dad has gone to sleep. 9. James has a bandage on his finger and he's in pain.Present Perfect: James has cut his finger.James has hurt his finger.

enriched.summary: A aula aborda o uso de diferentes tempos verbais para descrever ações em contextos específicos, além de apresentar vocabulário essencial relacionado a trabalho e situações cotidianas. Também inclui explicações sobre diferenças de pronúncia e exemplos práticos para fixação.
mainTopics: Vocabulário relacionado a trabalho e ações cotidianas

vocabulary.definition: A person responsible for the development and success of a product within a company.
examples: The product manager oversees the entire launch process.

vocabulary.definition: The act of bringing goods or services to a recipient.
examples: The delivery arrived on time.
We offer free delivery for orders over $50.

vocabulary.definition: To bring goods, letters, or packages to someone.
examples: The courier delivers the package every morning.
Can you deliver this message to John?

vocabulary.definition: To make a process operate automatically using machines or software.
examples: We need to automate this process to save time.
The company decided to automate its inventory system.

vocabulary.definition: A statement that tells what is allowed or what must be done in a particular situation.
examples: You must follow the rules of the game.
Breaking the rules will result in penalties.

vocabulary.definition: A function or part performed by a person or thing in a particular situation.
examples: Her role in the project was crucial.
He played the role of a mentor.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of money required to buy or do something.
examples: The cost of living has increased.
How much does it cost to travel to Europe?

vocabulary.definition: The land next to or near the sea.
examples: We spent the weekend at the coast.
The coast is a popular tourist destination.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving the desired aim or result.
examples: She is a successful entrepreneur.
The event was highly successful.

grammar.explanation: Used to describe actions that happened at an unspecified time in the past or have relevance to the present moment.
rules: Do not specify the exact time of the action.
examples: Sarah has cut her hair.
The floor has been cleaned.
Mark has sold his car.
commonMistakes: Using it with specific time indicators like 'yesterday' or 'last week'.

grammar.explanation: Used to describe actions that were in progress at a particular moment in the past.
rules: Often used with another action interrupting it.
examples: Sarah was cutting her hair when I arrived.
My sister was cleaning the floor when I arrived home.
commonMistakes: Using it without specifying the context.

expressions.usage: Used to describe a condition where success is achieved.
examples: If successful, the project will expand internationally.

practiceQuestions.question: Choose the correct tense: Sarah ______ her hair yesterday.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The action happened at a specific time in the past, so we use Past Simple.

practiceQuestions.question: Translate: Minha irmã limpou o chão ontem à noite.
practiceQuestions.answer: My sister cleaned the floor last night.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The action is in the past and specifies a time ('last night').

culturalNotes: In English-speaking countries, Present Perfect is often used to emphasize the result or connection of an action to the present moment.
The concept of 'role' can vary in workplace settings, often involving specific responsibilities tied to job titles.
studyTips: Practice identifying time indicators to choose the correct tense.
Use flashcards for vocabulary related to work and daily activities.
originalExamples: Sarah has cut her hair. (Sarah cortou o cabelo.)
The floor has been cleaned. (O chão foi limpo.)
Mark has sold his car. (Mark vendeu seu carro.)
My mother has baked a cake. (Minha mãe assou um bolo.)
They have lost their keys. (Eles perderam suas chaves.)
I have eaten all the food. (Eu comi toda a comida.)
My dad has gone to bed. (Meu pai foi dormir.)
James has cut his finger. (James cortou o dedo.)
